m12.motion:
Subtle handheld micro-movement, not shaky. He stays planted and raps straight into the lens. His finger taps his temple twice, quick and hard, then the hand snaps forward to point at the lens for a split second and drops straight back to his chest. His head gives four hard nods, his shoulders roll, and on the last nod his whole upper body drops forward and stops dead. Ambient sound: traffic rumbling across the flyover overhead. No speech or singing.

Thanks.

s01.motion:
Handheld camera an arm's length away, swinging a little with him. His clawed hand throws down past the lens, so fast it smears with motion blur, then snaps straight back up in front of his mask. He does it twice. Between throws his head dips forward and his shoulders hunch, the mask dropping in and out of the lamp's shadow. His feet stay put. Ambient sound: the wall vent humming and a distant siren. No speech or singing.

Thanks.

s02.motion:
Locked-off camera. His boots stay planted on the wet tarmac and his shadow stays joined to them. His knees bounce in four short hard dips. His flat right palm chops sideways at chest height and stops dead, chops back the other way and stops dead, then returns to his chest. His hips turn a little with each chop and his weight lands in his knees. Rainwater drips off the flyover edge. Ambient sound: tyres hissing overhead, water dripping. No speech or singing.

Thanks.

s03.motion:
A short push-in towards him over the first three seconds, then the camera holds still. He flicks his two pointing fingers down at the lens three times, quick and clipped, then his fist pumps down hard at waist height twice, stopping dead each time. His chest drops forward on every pump and his head bobs with it. Wind tugs at his jacket. Ambient sound: wind across the roof and the city humming below. No speech or singing.

Thanks.

s04.motion:
Locked-off camera. From the boxer's guard his right hand drops to chest height and rubs thumb against fingers, quick, twice, then slams down as a fist into his open left palm and stops dead. His shoulders jolt with the impact, his head nods hard three times, and his torso rocks forward towards the lens and back. His feet do not move. Ambient sound: the lamp buzzing, a bottle rolling on wet ground. No speech or singing.

Thanks.

s05.motion:
Subtle handheld camera, tiny natural micro-movements, not shaky. He raps hard straight into the lens. His head gives four quick, clipped nods and his shoulders roll; on every second nod his chest drops forward and lands. His raised fist pumps down at chest height twice, stopping dead each time, then one gloved finger presses his temple once and snaps back to his chest. His other hand keeps gripping his jacket. The mask stays the same size and the same shape. Sound: traffic rumbling overhead, wind flapping tent fabric.

Thanks.

s06.motion:
Locked-off camera. His feet stay planted on the wet paving; he does not step or walk, and his shadow stays joined to his boots. His knees give a small, quick bounce under heavy weight. His upturned palm jabs forward once at waist height, like a man asking, then snaps shut into a fist and pumps down twice, stopping dead. His other hand hangs by his thigh. His upper body rocks forward on each pump and his head bobs hard. Sound: river water lapping the wall, a distant siren.

Thanks.

t03.motion:
Locked-off camera. He raps down into the lens, leaning on his flat hand, and the tablecloth creases under his weight. His pointing finger flicks down at the floor three times, short and clipped, stopping dead each time, then returns to his waistcoat. His head gives small, curt nods and tips a little to one side, never past a quarter turn. His shoulders stay square, a contemptuous calm. Behind him the diners keep eating. Sound: cutlery on china, low murmured talk.

Thanks.

t04.motion:
A short push-in over the first three seconds, then the camera holds. His hand stays on the bar table, his weight leaning into it. His flat palm chops sideways at chest height four times, quick and hard, stopping dead on each chop, then flicks back over his shoulder in dismissal and returns to his lapel. His chin jerks up on each chop and his chest rocks forward. His head keeps facing the lens. Sound: wind across the terrace, glasses clinking, a distant helicopter.

Thanks.

t05.motion:
Subtle handheld micro-movement, not shaky. He stays planted, left hand gripping the rail, and rocks his chest forward towards the lens on each stressed word. His right index finger jabs straight down at the deck three times, quick and hard, stopping dead on each jab, then the hand snaps back to rest at his chest. Four sharp head nods. The deck rises and falls gently with the swell. Sound: engine rumble, wake hissing, wind across the deck.

Thanks.

t06.motion:
Handheld camera, very close, swinging slightly with him. His head tips back once as if laughing, then he ducks forward hard into the lens. His open right hand jerks up in front of his mask and is thrown down past the lens so fast it smears with motion blur, then comes back to his chest. Two hard nods, his shoulders rolling forward each time. His left hand stays against his jacket. Sound: surf breaking, palm fronds rattling in a warm wind.

Thanks.

t07.motion:
Locked-off camera. His feet stay planted on the concrete and the car takes his weight; his knees give a small tight bounce. His right fist pumps down at waist height four times, short and hard, stopping dead each time, while his left hand grips the edge of the car's wing. On the last pump he slaps his own jacket pocket flat with an open glove and leaves it there. His shadow stays joined to his shoes. Sound: ventilation hum, a distant car door thudding, tyres squeaking on a ramp.

Thanks.

t08.motion:
A slow, short push-in towards him. His right hand chops sideways at chest height twice, flat and clipped, stopping dead, then flicks backwards once from the wrist in a dismissive wave and drops to his chest. His upper body rocks forward on each chop. Then he lifts the champagne flute a few inches towards the lens in a small, smug toast and holds it still. The guests behind keep chatting. Sound: party murmur, glasses clinking, a light breeze in the trees.

Thanks.
